missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.

For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

When testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.

The retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall have an RI that does not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during the rotation about their axes ±5°, with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20'.

The retro-reflective devices shall have the resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters of Table A6-1: cycle 1 with a black-standard thermometer (65 ± 3 °C) or cycle 4 with a black-panel thermometer (63 ± 3 °C), exposure periods of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) or 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm), relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.

For all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, and the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON, the front or rear position lamp shall fulfill the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions.

The single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, except that these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.

When there is doubt, the requirement that no red light shall be emitted to the front and no white light shall be emitted to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; no account is taken of obstacles that were already present when the lamp was type-approved.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.
All categories of vehicles shall be equipped with two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except that this condition shall not apply to the optional rear lamps.

The rear position lamps shall be at a height above the ground of not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The horizontal angle of the lamp shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The vertical angle of the lamp shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

The electrical connections for rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11, except that if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
While daytime running lamps are not switched ON, the rear position lamp shall have a mandatory closed-circuit tell-tale.
The closed-circuit tell-tale of the rear position lamps shall be combined with that of the front position lamps; this requirement does not apply while the daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The geometric visibility of the retro-reflector shall have a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards.

The electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under this Regulation shall have an approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. affixed to it, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, the vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.

The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

For immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

For immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines; ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without a 12 V / 24 V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.
In the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii) in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The component shall have the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) affixed on it.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
The lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) shall have all measurements made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7 for luminous intensity and standard light distribution.
When reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps are operated for 1 minute and for 10 minutes, the luminous intensities shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensity distribution shall, depending on the light source technology and in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, where the luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

extra.text: Markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3. above need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.

extra.text: ESA(s) shall be tested for conducted emissions.

extra.text: ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.

extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a at the 12/24 V supply and connected lines; rear lamp functions meet the immunity performance criteria.

extra.text: Apply the test pulse 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 3b at the 12/24 V supply and connected lines; rear lamp functions meet the immunity performance criteria.

extra.text: Apply the starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
extra.test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile on the 12/24 V supply and connected lines; rear lamp functions meet the immunity performance criteria.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of marking against approval documents; pass if circled "E" with correct country number is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection; pass if a 4- to 6-digit sequential number matching the approval number is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection; pass if the function symbols per paragraph 3.2.4 for all approved functions are present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection; pass if "148R" followed by the correct two-digit series of amendments is present.

extra.text: The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of rear position lamps.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of lamp as mounted on vehicle; pass if arrow points outward from the vehicle.

extra.text: If applicable, to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4., the additional letter "D" shall be placed on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
extra.test_case: If lamp approved as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, visual inspection; pass if "D" is right of the relevant function symbol.

extra.text: If applicable, to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4., the additional letter "Y" shall be placed on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
extra.test_case: If lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system, visual inspection; pass if "Y" is right of the relevant function symbol.

extra.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution, see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3, the approval marking shall consist of a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
extra.test_case: If any function has reduced light distribution per Annex 3 para 1.1, visual inspection; pass if downward vertical arrow from horizontal segment is present.

extra.text: Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with non-replaceable light sources.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection; pass if rated voltage (e.g. 12V) or voltage range is marked on the lamp.

extra.text: The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.2. shall be affixed on the lamp.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection; pass if trade name/mark is on the lamp.

extra.text: The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.4. shall be affixed on the lamp.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection; pass if voltage marking is on the lamp.

extra.text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: If single approval mark is used, inspect lamp installed on vehicle; pass if mark is visible.

extra.text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
extra.test_case: If single approval mark is used, design review/disassembly check; pass if no light-transmitting part is removable without removing the approval mark.

extra.text: Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
extra.test_case: Verify conformity of each lamp function (rear position, stop, reversing) to all requirements of UN R148 paragraphs 4. and 5. by review of the test report against each sub-paragraph; pass if every applicable requirement in paragraphs 4. and 5. is met.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval shall apply to this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Document review against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes, using the series of amendments in force at the date of application. Pass if each applicable general and individual specification is verified as met.

extra.text: The requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Build a compliance matrix of the UN R48 requirements for each function on M1 vehicles, such as geometric visibility, colour and number. Check each item that can be verified at lamp type approval on the lamp or its drawings. Pass if all feasible items are verified compliant.

extra.text: An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D" is applicable to rear position lamps.
extra.test_case: Documentation and marking review: confirm that the "D" marking is used only if the rear position lamp function is an assembly of two independent lamps. Pass if the "D" marking appears only on an eligible function.

extra.text: An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D" is applicable to stop lamps.
extra.test_case: Documentation and marking review: confirm that the "D" marking is used only if the stop lamp function is an assembly of two independent lamps. Pass if the "D" marking appears only on an eligible function.

extra.text: An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable to rear position lamps.
extra.test_case: Documentation and marking review: confirm that the "Y" marking is used only if the rear position lamp function is an interdependent lamp system. Pass if the "Y" marking appears only on an eligible function.

extra.text: An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable to stop lamps.
extra.test_case: Documentation and marking review: confirm that the "Y" marking is used only if the stop lamp function is an interdependent lamp system. Pass if the "Y" marking appears only on an eligible function.

extra.text: Position lamps which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, are permitted.
extra.test_case: Design review of the circuit and light sources: if the rear position and stop functions share a common light source, confirm a permanently operating intensity-regulation system is fitted; then check photometry of both functions per R148.

extra.text: Stop lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the stop lamp's apparent surface, optics and outer lens. Pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: Reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the reversing lamp's apparent surface, optics and outer lens window. Pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.
extra.test_case: Review the circuit diagram and inspect the PCB wiring. Open-circuit one LED in each group and verify whether all LEDs of that group stop emitting. Pass: each group that fully extinguishes is treated as one light source in the failure assessment.

extra.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control (open or short the control input) while the lamp is in a state above the R1 maximum. Measure luminous intensity. Pass: the lamp automatically reverts to steady luminous intensity within the category requirements.

extra.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control while the lamp is in a state above the S1 maximum. Measure luminous intensity. Pass: the lamp automatically reverts to steady luminous intensity within the category requirements.

extra.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S4 emitting more than the maximum value of category S3, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control while the lamp is in a state above the S3 maximum. Measure luminous intensity. Pass: the lamp automatically reverts to steady luminous intensity within the category requirements.

extra.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
extra.test_case: Attempt to swap modules of different functions/characteristics within the housing, with tools; pass if not interchangeable

extra.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
extra.test_case: Confirm each function is measured in steady continuous operation, with no flashing or PWM start-up transient. Pass if readings are taken in continuous lit state.

extra.text: In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate the lamp through the applicant-specified control gear and supply conditions. Pass if the test conditions match the applicant's specification.

extra.text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate the lamp at the applicant-specified supply conditions. Pass if the test conditions match the specification.

extra.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.
extra.test_case: Measure each grid point where Annex 3 gives absolute values. Pass if each value is at least the specified intensity.

extra.text: In order to verify the visibility of white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No.48, the applicant may request an additional test, to show that in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction, the maximum intensity is not more than 2.5∙10-1cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometry over 165° to 180° outboard H and -2.5° to +5° V, optionally with vehicle body influence. Pass if the maximum is at most 0.25 cd.

extra.text: If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously at the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
extra.test_case: Measure the rear position lamp alone, then position and stop lamps together, at all grid points within ±5° V and ±10° H. Pass if the combined-to-alone ratio is at least 5:1 at each point.

extra.text: If one or both of the two reciprocally incorporated lamps contain(s) more than one light source and is (are) considered as a single lamp, the values to be considered are those obtained with all sources in operation.
extra.test_case: Perform the ratio measurement with all LEDs of each function energised. Pass if the 5:1 ratio is met.

extra.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
extra.test_case: Measure colour with the LED light sources installed in the lamp, per relevant subparagraphs of 4.8; pass if chromaticity within limits.

extra.text: The minimum luminous intensity of rear position lamps of category R1 (steady) shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on reference axis per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a); pass if ≥ 4 cd

extra.text: The maximum luminous intensity of rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), when used as a single lamp, shall be 1.7∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan of the full light distribution per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if ≤ 17 cd in all directions (≤ 60 cd below 5° down if reciprocally incorporated with stop lamp)

extra.text: The maximum luminous intensity of rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), when used as a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), shall be 8.5∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Only if the lamp is marked "D": goniophotometer scan per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if ≤ 8.5 cd

extra.text: The minimum luminous intensity of rear position lamps of category R2 (variable) shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Only if the lamp is category R2: goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a); pass if ≥ 4 cd

extra.text: The maximum luminous intensity of rear position lamps of category R2 (variable), when used as a single lamp, shall be 4.2∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Only if the lamp is category R2: goniophotometer scan per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if ≤ 42 cd

extra.text: The maximum luminous intensity of rear position lamps of category R2 (variable), when used as a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), shall be 2.1∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Only if the lamp is category R2 and marked "D": goniophotometer scan per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if ≤ 21 cd

extra.text: The standard light distribution of rear position lamps shall be as defined in Figure A3-I and Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure grid points of Figure A3-I and compare with Table A2-1 percentages per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(c); pass if each point meets its requirement

extra.text: The minimum luminous intensity of rear position lamps within the angles of geometric visibility (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) shall be 5∙10^-2 cd.
extra.test_case: Measure across the geometric visibility angles per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d); pass if ≥ 0.05 cd in all directions

extra.text: A luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted for rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan below 5° down from horizontal; pass if ≤ 60 cd in that region (Table 4 maximum elsewhere)

extra.text: Failure provisions for rear position lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Simulate light source failure per paragraph 4.6; pass if paragraph 4.6 criteria are met

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 3 on both samples; intensity at the reference axis/test points ≥ 60 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) when used as a single lamp shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement on both samples; no direction exceeds 260 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) when used as a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.) shall be 1.30∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: If marked "D": goniophotometric measurement on both samples; no direction exceeds 130 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the angles of geometric visibility (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) shall be as defined in Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Verify geometric visibility angles against Figure A3-I.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) shall be as defined in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure at test points of Table A2-1; values meet the prescribed percentages of minimum intensity.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility shall be 3∙10^-1 cd.
extra.test_case: Measure throughout the Figure A3-I field; intensity ≥ 0.3 cd everywhere.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement on both samples; intensity ≥ 60 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) when used as a single lamp shall be 7.30∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement on both samples; no direction exceeds 730 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) when used as a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.) shall be 3.65∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: If marked "D": goniophotometric measurement; no direction exceeds 365 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the angles of geometric visibility (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) shall be as defined in Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Verify geometric visibility angles against Figure A3-I.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) shall be as defined in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure at test points of Table A2-1; values meet prescribed percentages.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility shall be 3∙10^-1 cd (day).
extra.test_case: Day condition: measure throughout Figure A3-I field; intensity ≥ 0.3 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7: for a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility shall be 7∙10^-2 cd (night).
extra.test_case: Night condition: measure throughout Figure A3-I field; intensity ≥ 0.07 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10: the minimum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) for reversing lamps of category AR shall be 8.0∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of both samples per para 4.8.3.1 (a); pass if intensity ≥ 80 cd where minimum applies.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10: the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) for reversing lamps of category AR in or above the H-plane shall be 3.00∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan of both samples in and above the H-plane; pass if no value exceeds 300 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10: the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) for reversing lamps of category AR below the H-plane, down to 5°D, shall be 6.00∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan of both samples from H-plane down to 5°D; pass if no value exceeds 600 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10: the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) for reversing lamps of category AR below 5°D shall be 8.00∙10^3 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer scan of both samples below 5°D; pass if no value exceeds 8000 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10: the standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) for reversing lamps of category AR shall be as defined in Figure A3-V.
extra.test_case: Measure both samples at the grid points of Figure A3-V; pass if each point meets the specified percentage of the minimum intensity.

extra.text: In the case where the type approval is granted applying the pair condition, the device shall only be installed in a pair.
extra.test_case: Vehicle inspection: verify the pair-only approved reversing lamp is fitted as a left/right pair.

extra.text: Front/rear position (A, R1, R2): minimum horizontal angles (inboard / outboard) 45°/80°.
extra.test_case: Geometric visibility check of the apparent surface on a goniometer with the lamp in its mounting orientation. Pass if the apparent surface is visible over at least 45° inboard and 80° outboard.

extra.text: Front/rear position (A, R1, R2): minimum horizontal angles (inboard / outboard) (20°/80°), reduced angles used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
extra.test_case: If the H-plane mounting height is below 750 mm, verify visibility below the H-plane over at least 20° inboard and 80° outboard. Pass if the apparent surface is visible over these angles.

extra.text: Front/rear position (A, R1, R2): minimum vertical angles (above / below) 15°/15°.
extra.test_case: Geometric visibility check in the vertical plane. Pass if the apparent surface is visible from 15° above to 15° below the H-plane.

extra.text: Front/rear position (A, R1, R2): minimum vertical angles (above / below) (15°/5°) for lamps to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.
extra.test_case: If the mounting height is below 750 mm, verify vertical visibility. Pass if the apparent surface is visible from 15° above to 5° below the H-plane.

extra.text: Stop lamp (S1, S2): minimum horizontal angles (inboard / outboard) 45°/45°.
extra.test_case: Geometric visibility check of the stop lamp apparent surface on a goniometer. Pass if the apparent surface is visible over at least 45° inboard and 45° outboard.

extra.text: Stop lamp (S1, S2): minimum horizontal angles (inboard / outboard) (20°/45°), reduced angles used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
extra.test_case: If the H-plane is below 750 mm, verify visibility below the H-plane. Pass if the apparent surface is visible over at least 20° inboard and 45° outboard.

extra.text: Stop lamp (S1, S2): minimum vertical angles (above / below) 15°/15°.
extra.test_case: Vertical geometric visibility check. Pass if the apparent surface is visible from 15° above to 15° below the H-plane.

extra.text: Stop lamp (S1, S2): minimum vertical angles (above / below) (15°/5°) for lamps to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.
extra.test_case: If the mounting height is below 750 mm, verify vertical visibility. Pass if the apparent surface is visible from 15° above to 5° below the H-plane.

extra.text: Unless specified otherwise, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement at the Annex 3 grid points; compute the % of the required minimum, rounded down to 3 significant digits; each point must meet or exceed the value.

extra.text: In the case where rear position lamps are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the manufacturer's H-plane mounting height. If ≤ 750 mm, limit downward photometric verification to V = -5°.

extra.text: In the case where stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the manufacturer's H-plane mounting height. If ≤ 750 mm, limit downward photometric verification of the S1/S2 stop lamp to V = -5°.

extra.text: For rear position lamps, the values shown in Figure A3-I give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8).
extra.test_case: Photometry at the Figure A3-I points. The intensity must be ≥ the stated % of the required minimum.

extra.text: For stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS), the values shown in Figure A3-I give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8).
extra.test_case: Photometry at the Figure A3-I points. The intensity must be ≥ the stated % of the Table 7 minimum.

extra.text: For reversing lamps, the values shown in figure A3-V give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities in cd.
extra.test_case: Photometry at the Figure A3-V points relative to the axis of reference. The intensity must be ≥ the cd value shown.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement under conditions of paragraph 4.9 of UN R148; pass if chromaticity coordinates are within the prescribed colour limits

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: CoP colorimetric measurement under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148; pass if chromaticity coordinates are within the prescribed colour boundaries.

extra.text: The following approval marking arrangements are given merely as examples and any other arrangement made in accordance with paragraph 3.3. of this Regulation is acceptable.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the approval marking on the lamp against paragraph 3.3. of UN R148 (Annex 7 examples for reference); pass if the arrangement complies with paragraph 3.3.

extra.text: For reversing lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.1: operate the reversing function and measure luminous intensity distribution after 1 min and 10 min of operation, or calculate it from the distribution after photometric stability using the HV ratios. Pass if all test points are at or above the minimum values.

extra.text: For reversing lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.1 after 1 min and 10 min of operation, measured directly or calculated using the HV ratios. Pass if no test point exceeds the maximum values.

extra.text: For all other lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2 after 1 min and after either 30 min of operation or photometric stability. Pass if no test point exceeds the maximum values, including the stop and position lamp maximums.

extra.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking the value for “a” is defined in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimensions; the size of “a” must be at least the Table 1 value.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: a circle surrounding "E" and the distinguishing country number are present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: a 4–6 digit sequential number matching the approval number is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: the class symbol per paragraph 3.2.5 (e.g. IA) is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter “R” and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: the marking contains "150R" followed by the correct two-digit series number.

extra.text: Retro-reflective devices shall bear, in case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the word “TOP” inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Review the manufacturer's rotation specification. If orientation is not unambiguous, "TOP" must be inscribed horizontally at the highest part of the illuminating surface.

extra.text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed. This marking may be located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Install the lamp on the vehicle or a representative fixture; the single mark must be visible.

extra.text: This marking may be located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
extra.test_case: Design review and disassembly check: no light-transmitting part (outer lens, reversing window, retro-reflector) can be removed without also removing the mark.

extra.text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
extra.test_case: Test production samples of the retro-reflector against the requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5. (photometric, colorimetric and other specifications); pass if the samples meet them and conform to the approved type.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval shall apply to this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Document review: confirm that the retro-reflector satisfies UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and the Annexes they reference, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application. Pass if every applicable item verifiable at component level is met.

extra.text: The requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Review the UN R48 requirements for rear retro-reflectors on M1 vehicles, such as geometric visibility angles and orientation. Verify those that can be checked at device approval, using drawings and goniometric or visual inspection of the mounting reference. Pass if all feasible pertinent requirements are met.

extra.text: Any protuberances the outer surface of retro-reflective devices may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
extra.test_case: Inspection of any protuberances on the outer surface; pass if they do not hinder cleaning.

extra.text: The colouring of filters by means of paint or varnish is not permitted.
extra.test_case: Material specification review and inspection; pass if filter colour is obtained without paint or varnish.

extra.text: For testing the daytime colour, the material shall be illuminated by the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664- 2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0) or (0:45a) as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Daytime colour test per Annex 4 Part 2: illuminate the material with CIE D65 using (45a:0) or (0:45a) geometry and measure the chromaticity. Pass if the set-up conforms and the measured colour lies within the specified daytime colour limits.

extra.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in the paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
extra.test_case: Colorimetry per paragraph 4.2. after each test group, using trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt. Pass: red night-time colour limits of UN R48.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA, IB must be equal to or greater than 3.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 for an angle of divergence of 20' at illumination angles β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0°. Pass: RI of at least 300 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA, IB must be equal to or greater than 2.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 for an angle of divergence of 20' at illumination angles β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20', β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°. Pass: RI of at least 200 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA, IB must be equal to or greater than 1.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 for an angle of divergence of 20' at illumination angles β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
extra.test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20', β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°. Pass: RI of at least 100 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA, IB must be equal to or greater than 5∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 for an angle of divergence of 1°30' at illumination angles β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 1°30', β1 = β2 = 0°. Pass: RI of at least 5 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA, IB must be equal to or greater than 2.8∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 for an angle of divergence of 1°30' at illumination angles β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 1°30', β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°. Pass: RI of at least 2.8 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA, IB must be equal to or greater than 2.5∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 for an angle of divergence of 1°30' at illumination angles β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
extra.test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 1°30', β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°. Pass: RI of at least 2.5 mcd/lx.

extra.text: In the case where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the declared mounting height. If the H plane is below 750 mm, verify RI downward only to 5°. Pass: Table 3 minima met within the applicable range.

extra.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux must be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
extra.test_case: Trichromatic coordinate measurement of the reflected light. Pass: coordinates within the UN R48 red night-time colour boundaries.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples per R150; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed red boundaries.

extra.text: In any test of conformity carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used with the consent of the Type Approval Authority.
extra.test_case: If alternative methods are used, verify Type Approval Authority consent and manufacturer's proof of equivalence.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production retro-reflector samples; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed red colour limits of R150.

extra.text: If the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 1.2: if values are not met, rotate ±5° from the minimum-RI position; pass if specified values are attained within that range.

extra.text: The RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 1.3: record RI continuously during the ±5° rotation; pass if RI ≥ the prescribed value at every position.

extra.text: For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 3.3: verify source calibrated to CIE Standard Illuminant A and the procedure of Annex 4 Part 1 is followed.

extra.text: In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 1 para. 1 heat resistance: condition sample in dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 consecutive hours; verify chamber temperature log and duration.

extra.text: After this test, no appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component must be visible.
extra.test_case: Visual/dimensional inspection after Annex 6 Part 1 heat test and cooling: pass if no appreciable distortion visible on retro-reflector body or optical component.

extra.text: Retro-reflective devices whether part of a lamp or not shall be immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: immerse for 10 min in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface; then assess per para 1.2.

extra.text: The immersion test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: repeat the 10 min / 50 °C ± 5 °C immersion inverted, illuminating surface down, rear face under about 20 mm of water.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: immediately after the 50 °C immersions, immerse under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C; then assess per paras 1.2 and 1.3.

extra.text: If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.2: visual inspection after immersion; fail if water is clearly visible at the reflecting surface.

extra.text: As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the following tests (moisture and dust test) shall be applied.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 3: apply the moisture test (para. 2) and the dust exposure test (para. 2.3) on manufacturer request; pass if both evaluations are met.

extra.text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
extra.test_case: Water spray test para. 2.2.3: operate the lamp functions at design voltage, 5 min ON / 55 min OFF; pass if the cycle is applied throughout.

extra.text: The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
extra.test_case: Water spray test para. 2.2.4: verify the duration; pass if 12 h, 12 cycles.

extra.text: No standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed, or which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
extra.test_case: Water spray test para. 2.2.6: inspect, tap and tilt the device; pass if no standing pool of water is present or formed.

extra.text: The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours.
extra.test_case: Dust test para. 2.3.6: verify an agitation of 2–15 s every 15 min over 5 h; pass if the schedule is met.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
extra.test_case: Remove all removable parts; salt mist exposure 24 h + 2 h drying + 24 h (50 h total); verify test sequence recorded.

extra.text: The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9.
extra.test_case: After 48 h recovery, measure RA per Annex 6 Part 2 at β2 = 5°, α = 20'; pass if RA ≥ Table 9 value.

extra.text: The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not more than the value in Table 10.
extra.test_case: After 48 h recovery, measure RA per Annex 6 Part 2 at β2 = 5°, α = 20'; pass if RA ≤ Table 10 value.

extra.text: A test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied for a retro-reflective device.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 Part 1: Confirm the test mixture is 70 vol.% n-heptane and 30 vol.% toluol before testing the retro-reflector. Pass if the mixture composition matches.

extra.text: The surface of the retro-reflective device must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 Part 1 para 1.1(b): After the fuel wipe and a wait of about 5 minutes, visually inspect the surface. Pass if there are no apparent surface changes; slight surface cracks are acceptable.

extra.text: The approval number must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark on the retro-reflective device against Annex 10 Figure A10-I: the approval number is located adjacent to the circle surrounding "E".

extra.text: The digits constituting the approval number must face the same way as the "E".
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark: the approval number digits have the same orientation as the letter "E".

extra.text: The group of symbols indicating the class must be diametrically opposite the approval number.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark: the class symbol (e.g. IA) is positioned diametrically opposite the approval number relative to the circle.

extra.text: For all light-signalling devices, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road.
extra.test_case: Measure the reference axis of each installed function relative to the vehicle's bearing plane on the road; pass if parallel within ±3°.

extra.text: The reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle in the case of all other signalling devices.
extra.test_case: Measure the reference axis of each installed function relative to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane; pass if parallel within ±3°.

extra.text: In each direction a tolerance of ±3° shall be allowed.
extra.test_case: Measure the angular deviation of the reference axis in the vertical and horizontal directions; pass if each deviation is within ±3°.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).
extra.test_case: Inspect the vehicle drawings and the installed vehicle, and measure the lateral positions of the exterior geometrical form of the LH and RH housings/outer lenses relative to the median longitudinal plane. Pass if they are symmetrical.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
extra.test_case: Compare the LH and RH unit drawings/CAD and the physical samples, mirrored about the median longitudinal plane, ignoring interior structure. Pass if the exterior shapes are mirror-symmetrical.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
extra.test_case: Perform colorimetric measurement of each function on the LH and RH samples according to the device regulation (e.g. UN R148/R150 or R7/R23/R3). Pass if both sides meet the same colour requirement (red for position/stop/retro-reflector, white for reversing).

extra.text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical the above requirements shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
extra.test_case: Installation inspection per UN R48 on an M1 vehicle with asymmetrical external shape: check that the preceding installation requirements (e.g. symmetrical pairing, position, geometric visibility) are met as far as the body shape allows, and that any deviation is justified by the asymmetry.

extra.text: When a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamps are switched ON.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the stop lamp (red) with the rear position lamp and stop lamp switched ON simultaneously. Pass if the chromaticity coordinates are within the red colour boundaries of R48 para 5.11 / R148.

extra.text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that: (a) Either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) The minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
extra.test_case: Project the distinct parts of the apparent surface along the reference axis onto a plane tangent to the outer lens (CAD/drawing measurement). Pass if projected area >= 60 % of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or the gap between facing edges of adjacent parts <= 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.

extra.text: The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
extra.test_case: Measure photometry and colour of each function with the other functions of the module switched ON and OFF in all combinations. Pass if every state complies with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned, including the intensity ratio of stop lamp to position lamp.

extra.text: The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
extra.test_case: Measure photometry and colour for each function provided by the shared light sources, e.g. LEDs serving both the position and stop functions at different intensities. Pass if each function meets its own regulation requirements.

extra.text: For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
extra.test_case: Visual/geometric check on vehicle: observer moves within Zone 1 of Annex 4 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle; pass if no part of the apparent surface of any red lamp is directly visible.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp is the following: White.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the light emitted by the reversing lamp through the outer lens window (spectroradiometer/colorimeter, CIE 1931 coordinates) at rated voltage; pass if chromaticity (x,y) lies within the white boundaries W12–W61 defined in the Regulation.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp is the following: Red.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the light emitted by the stop lamp through the outer lens at rated voltage; pass if chromaticity (x,y) lies within the red chromaticity area defined in the Regulation.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp is the following: Red.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the light emitted by the rear position lamp through the outer lens at rated voltage; pass if chromaticity (x,y) lies within the red chromaticity area defined in the Regulation.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is the following: Red.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric check of the retro-reflected light under CIE standard illuminant A illumination per the retro-reflector device regulation; pass if chromaticity lies within the red chromaticity area.

extra.text: The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the M1 vehicle installation against the individual specifications of UN R48 (paragraphs 6.x for each function); pass if the number of rear position, stop, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors fitted equals the number indicated (e.g. 2 rear position lamps, 2 stop lamps, 1 or 2 reversing lamps, 2 rear retro-reflectors).

extra.text: Any lamp may be installed on movable components provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.
extra.test_case: Installation inspection of the vehicle drawings and the vehicle: determine whether any lamp function or the retro-reflector is mounted on a movable component. If none is, record the provision as not applicable to this body-mounted unit. If any is, verify compliance with paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. Pass if the lamp is body-mounted or if all three referenced conditions are met.

extra.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of rear position lamps shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".
extra.test_case: Vehicle inspection: place each movable component in every fixed position (stable or natural rest positions specified by the manufacturer, locked or not) other than the normal position of use; measure the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis; pass if ≤50 per cent is hidden.

extra.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".
extra.test_case: Vehicle inspection: place each movable component in every manufacturer-specified fixed position other than the normal position of use; measure the apparent surface of the retro-reflector in the direction of the reference axis; pass if ≤50 per cent is hidden.

extra.text: If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.
extra.test_case: Where >50 per cent hiding occurs: verify additional lamps meet position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps and are switched ON automatically whenever the movable component hides >50 per cent of the apparent surface; pass if both conditions met.

extra.text: If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for retro-reflectors shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these retro-reflectors is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.
extra.test_case: Where >50 per cent hiding of the retro-reflector occurs: verify additional devices meet position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements and are active when the movable component hides >50 per cent; pass if met.

extra.text: If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road; for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.
extra.test_case: Vehicle inspection: where the rear position lamp apparent surface can be >50 per cent hidden and no additional lamps are provided, check presence of the user notice in the vehicle with the required content; pass if present.

extra.text: With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark is deemed not to be present when the lamp cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.
extra.test_case: Inspection of the lamp as installed on the vehicle: with the vehicle wiring and connector as delivered, confirm that each of the rear position, stop and reversing functions operates when only a light source and/or fuse is installed. Pass if every function operates without any other modification; otherwise that function is deemed not present.

extra.text: Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of rear position lamp LEDs; verify replacement function emits red light, with intensity per R7 rear position lamp values and from comparable position (within the same lamp/apparent surface area); pass if colour, main intensity and position are similar.

extra.text: Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement device remains operational in its original safety function.
extra.test_case: With rear position lamp failure simulated and replacement active, activate the replacement device's original function (e.g. braking); pass if original function operates with required photometry and is distinguishable.

extra.text: During replacement, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.
extra.test_case: Simulate rear position lamp failure on vehicle; pass if dashboard tell-tale activates indicating temporary replacement and need for repair for the full duration of replacement.

extra.text: Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, which respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., are allowed, provided that the intensity of all the lamps mentioned above, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
extra.test_case: Functional test across the intensity control range: measure the intensity of the R2 and S2 functions at several control steps and confirm they vary together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

extra.text: Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control are allowed, provided that in the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of the stop and rear position lamp intensities during transitions across the full range; the prescribed stop/position intensity ratio (where applicable) is maintained at every point.

extra.text: Increase and decrease of the luminous intensity, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed in relation to the following conditions: ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds, contamination of the light emitting surface.
extra.test_case: Review of the control strategy: intensity variation is triggered only by the listed environmental conditions. Photometry at the minimum and maximum settings stays within the R2/S2 limits of the pertinent UN Regulation.

extra.text: Independent from environmental conditions mentioned under 5.26.1. a decrease of the luminous intensity, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m.
